expected.name: Herman Rohde
expected.description: Herman Rohde was a German-born farmer in the Pine Hills area of Custer County. In 1918 he was convicted of sedition for remarks about Germany, American troops and the war, receiving a four-to-eight-year sentence. He was imprisoned at Deer Lodge and released on April 17, 1921. He died in Oregon in 1923.

operations.name: James Rolf Bjerkan

expected.charges: Refusing to report for induction, 50 U.S.C. App. section 462(a).
expected.convicted: Conviction affirmed March 9, 1973; full unconditional presidential pardon December 28, 1974.
expected.sentence: Three years, reduced to eighteen months on January 4, 1974. Held at the federal correctional institution at Sandstone, Minnesota. Furloughed before the November 6, 1974 habeas ruling; exact departure date unverified. The December 28 pardon is not the custody endpoint.

updates.prosecutor: Samuel K. Skinner; Michael D. Groark (government counsel on 1975 appeal)
